target_customer: Patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, ultimately reached through pharma partners and prescribers
problem: Existing obesity and diabetes drugs do not address the imbalance between calorie intake and expenditure; the company aims to increase energy expenditure by activating mitochondrial heat production.
business_model: Drug discovery biotech seeking to develop and out-license or commercialize a first in class small molecule
product_category: Therapeutics, obesity and metabolic disease (mitochondrial thermogenesis)

founders.name: Jonah Sinick
education: PhD (institution not stated on company site)
founders.background_notes: Listed as Co-Founder and CEO on the company website.

founders.name: Yuriy Kirichok
education: PhD (institution not stated on company site)
founders.background_notes: Company site lists foundational papers including a 2019 Nature paper on the ADP/ATP carrier; an NIH grant record credits the co-founders with that finding.

founders.name: Liliya Khasin
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only; not on the company team page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires identifying a molecular target, running a high throughput screen and developing a safe small molecule through clinical trials; earlier uncouplers had toxicity problems.

defensibility.rationale: A novel target and screening platform with published science could be protective if a drug works, but no patents or licensing were verified in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GLP-1 incumbents dominated obesity drugs; no evidence found that any incumbent targeted this mechanism or acquired Equator.

market_need_then: The YC description cites 2.2B overweight people and 500M with type 2 diabetes worldwide and says existing drugs are not effective enough; these are company claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses equatortherapeutics.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific with a slogan, Restoring thermogenesis to prehistoric levels

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Restoring thermogenesis to prehistoric levels

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand was found; it is a science led biotech with minimal public presence.

outcome_analysis: Equator Therapeutics is a very small, science led obesity drug developer from YC Winter 2020 that remains active with a small team and public funding signals limited to grants and aggregator listed small rounds. It has not shown clinical stage progress in public sources opened, so its outcome is still pending rather than a success or failure. The long timelines and capital needs of drug development are the main risk.
notes: Funding figures from aggregators conflict and are unverified, so not recorded as rounds: Seedtable lists a $150K convertible note on 2020-03-16, Employbl lists a $125K seed from BioGenerator Ventures and others, other listings show a $500K 2022 round led by Alameda Research, and one lists a $1.91M HHS grant dated 2021-09-20. Total raised ranges from $125K to $1.15M across sources. The NIH grant record was seen only in search results; its amount and date were not read. The company site gives St. Louis, Missouri while YC lists San Francisco. Sources disagree on founders (Employbl adds Michael Grabe, who appears on the company's science advisory board). No competitor source dated near the 2020 batch was found; Rivus Pharmaceuticals pursued a related uncoupler approach but its Series A was announced July 2021, so it is excluded. Outcome searches found nothing on acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Founding year not stated in sources.
